title: Module sheaves are generated by extension-by-zero free modules
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site (its objects and morphisms form sets) and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and let $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ be the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ let $j_U:\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal C$ be the localization morphism, $\mathcal O_U$ the restriction of $\mathcal O$ to $\mathcal C/U$, and $j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$ the extension by zero, so that a section $s\in\mathcal M(U)$ of a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal M$ corresponds to the morphism $j_{U!}\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal M$ adjoint to $\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal M|_U$, $1\mapsto s$. Then for every sheaf $\mathcal M$ of $\mathcal O$-modules the coproduct $\bigoplus_{(U,s)}j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$, indexed by the set of pairs $(U,s)$ with $U$ an object of $\mathcal C$ and $s\in\mathcal M(U)$, exists, and the morphism $\bigoplus_{(U,s)}j_{U!}\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal M$ whose $(U,s)$ component is the morphism attached to $s$ is an epimorphism.

source.place: Lemma 18.28.8 (Tag 03EW), clause (3), every sheaf module is a quotient of a direct sum of j_{U!}O_U

proof.text: For an object $U$ let $P_U$ be the extension-by-zero presheaf of $\mathcal O_U$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf], so $P_U(V)=\bigoplus_{\varphi\in\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(V,U)}\mathcal O(V)$ with $\mathcal O(V)$ acting summandwise, and $j_{U!}\mathcal O_U=P_U^\#$ with $\theta_U:P_U\to P_U^\#$ its sheafification as a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. By the universal property of $\theta_U$, $\psi\mapsto\psi\circ\theta_U$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(j_{U!}\mathcal O_U,\mathcal M)$ onto the $\mathcal O$-linear presheaf maps $P_U\to\mathcal M$. Write $1_\varphi\in P_U(V)$ for the unit in the summand of $\varphi:V\to U$; by the restriction rule of [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf], $1_\varphi$ is the restriction of $1_{\mathrm{id}_U}\in P_U(U)$ along $\varphi$, and the $1_\varphi$ generate $P_U(V)$ over $\mathcal O(V)$. Hence an $\mathcal O$-linear $g:P_U\to\mathcal M$ is determined by $g_U(1_{\mathrm{id}_U})$, via $g_V(\sum_\varphi a_\varphi1_\varphi)=\sum_\varphi a_\varphi\,\mathcal M(\varphi)(g_U(1_{\mathrm{id}_U}))$, and conversely for each $s\in\mathcal M(U)$ this formula defines an $\mathcal O$-linear presheaf map (compatibility with restriction along $a:V'\to V$ holds since $1_\varphi|_{V'}=1_{\varphi a}$ and $\mathcal M(\varphi a)=\mathcal M(a)\mathcal M(\varphi)$). So $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(j_{U!}\mathcal O_U,\mathcal M)\cong\mathcal M(U)$, $\psi\mapsto(\psi\theta_U)_U(1_{\mathrm{id}_U})$ (Stacks 03ES/03EW proof). For $s\in\mathcal M(U)$ let $\alpha_{U,s}:j_{U!}\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal M$ be the morphism corresponding to $s$; it satisfies $(\alpha_{U,s})_U(\theta_U(1_{\mathrm{id}_U}))=s$. Since $\mathcal C$ is small the pairs $(U,s)$ form a set.

source.place: Lemma 18.28.8 (Tag 03EW), proof of clause (3), first paragraph

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] (2) (a small site satisfies its sheafification hypothesis, and a set is a small discrete index category), the coproduct $\bigoplus_{(U,s)}j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$ exists in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$; it is the sheafification of the sectionwise direct sum, with coprojections $\iota_{U,s}$. Its universal property gives a unique $q:\bigoplus_{(U,s)}j_{U!}\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal M$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ with $q\circ\iota_{U,s}=\alpha_{U,s}$ for all $(U,s)$. In particular $q_U(\iota_{U,s,U}(\theta_U(1_{\mathrm{id}_U})))=s$.

source.place: Lemma 18.28.8 (Tag 03EW), proof of clause (3), direct-sum construction

proof.text: For any object $V$ and section $t\in\mathcal M(V)$, the pair $(V,t)$ is an index, and the preceding step gives an element of $(\bigoplus_{(U,s)}j_{U!}\mathcal O_U)(V)$ that $q_V$ sends to $t$. So every $q_V$ is surjective: the sectionwise cokernel $V\mapsto\mathcal M(V)/q_V(\cdot)$ is zero. In the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] the cokernel of $q$ is the sheafification of the sectionwise cokernel ([def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] (1)), the sheafification of the zero presheaf, hence $0$. A morphism with zero cokernel in an abelian category is an epimorphism, so $q$ is an epimorphism.
